body.p: Favorable reconsideration and allowance of this application are requested.
1. Discussion of Amendments
By way of the amendment instructions above, the pending claims herein have been amended in the interests of clarity and to advance prosecution of this application to allowance.

In this regard, it will be observed that independent claims 1 and 8 have each been amended to as to improve syntax and to further define the floating nut plate assemblies as having a "one piece U-shaped nut plate body" which is comprised of:
(i) a pair of circumferentially spaced-apart support legs having opposed first
and second ends, wherein the first end of each of the support legs is
rigidly joined to a lower surface of the inner cover plate and thereby
dependently extend from the inner cover plate toward the outer cover
plate, and
(ii) a planar nut plate which is structurally connected to and thereby bridges
the second ends of each of the support legs, wherein
(iii) the planar nut plate is in alignment with a respective one of the apertures
defined by the outer cover plate and is adapted to threadably receive a
respective one of the attachments bolts extending therethrough.
Support for the amendments can be found throughout the originally filed specification, see e.g., paragraph [0020] and FIGS. 3-6.
Claims 2 and 9 have been canceled to prevent redundancy. Several adjustments have been made to the remaining dependent claims to align the language thereof with the amendments made to claims 1 and 8.
Certain clerical errors have been corrected in paragraph [0020] of the specification.

Following entry of this amendment, therefore, claims 1, 3-8 and 10-16 will remain pending herein for consideration. As will become evident from the following discussion, all pending claims herein are in condition for allowance.
2. Claim Rejections - 35 USC §§102 and 103
The only issues to be resolved in this application are the following art-based rejections that were advanced against the prior pending claims herein:
Claim(s) 1-6 is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) as being
anticipated by Beijing Aeronautical Science & Technology Research
(BASTR) (EP 3998193 A).
Claim(s) 8-13 and 16 is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) as being
anticipated by Beijing Aeronautical Science & Technology Research
(BASTR) (EP 3998193 A).
Claim(s) 7 is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over
Beijing Aeronautical Science & Technology Research (BASTR) (EP
3998193 A) in view of Ramirez et al. (US 20090294591 A1).
Claim(s) 14-15 is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable
over Beijing Aeronautical Science & Technology Research (BASTR) (EP
3998193 A) in view of Ramirez et al. (US 20090294591 A1).
Applicant submits that the applied references of record are inappropriate to reject the amended claims now pending herein under 35 USC §§102 or 103.

In this regard, the Applicant notes that the presently claimed invention is directed to a novel and unobvious access cover panel assembly that includes floating nut plate assemblies each having a "one piece U-shaped nut plate body" which is comprised of:
(i) a pair of circumferentially spaced-apart support legs having opposed first
and second ends, wherein the first end of each of the support legs is rigidly joined to a lower surface of the inner cover plate and thereby
dependently extend from the inner cover plate toward the outer cover
plate, and
(ii) a planar nut plate which is structurally connected to and thereby bridges
the second ends of each of the support legs, wherein
(iii) the planar nut plate is in alignment with a respective one of the apertures
defined by the outer cover plate and is adapted to threadably receive a
respective one of the attachments bolts extending therethrough.
Such structures as shown in the drawing Figures of this application with FIGS. 3 and 6 being reproduced below for convenience:

The Applicant acknowledges that the BASTR EP publication indeed discloses an airplane wing fuel tank access cover. It is really at this juncture that any perceived similarities between the access cover disclosed by the BASTR EP publication and the access cover as claimed herein cease.

In this regard, the Examiner is apparently using the elements shown in FIG. 9 of the BASTR EP publication as disclosing certain of the previously claimed element. For example, the Examiner considers the BASTR EP publication to show by the vertical and lower horizontal segments of the elements 73 in FIG. 9 a structure which is structurally similar to the previously claimed "U-shaped floating nut plate assemblies". Applicant respectfully disagrees with such an interpretation.
FIG. 9 of the BASTR EP publication is reproduced below for convenience:

The specification of the BASTR EP publication refers to element 73 as a
"sandwich layer" which can be a "honeycomb" positioned between the "inner filler cap

interior skin 71" and the "sunken inner filler cap skin 76" as is shown in FIGS. 5-7. As described in paragraph [0027], such a structure is a "...foam sandwich structure [which] is composed of two rigid panels and a foam core sandwiched therebetween." Element 73 therefore cannot constitute a plurality of individual floating nut plate assemblies, each of which includes a one-piece U-shaped nut plate body having the structural characteristics of:
(i) a pair of circumferentially spaced-apart support legs having opposed first
and second ends, wherein the first end of each of the support legs is
rigidly joined to a lower surface of the inner cover plate and thereby
dependently extend from the inner cover plate toward the outer cover
plate, and
(ii) a planar nut plate which is structurally connected to and thereby bridges
the second ends of each of the support legs, wherein
(iii) the planar nut plate is in alignment with a respective one of the apertures
defined by the outer cover plate and is adapted to threadably receive a
respective one of the attachments bolts extending therethrough.
Applicant also notes that the BASTR EP publication discloses in paragraph

[0032] that an element 78 may be provided and can be either an L-shaped piece or a U- shaped piece formed of a composite or metal structure. Such structures are, however, not adapted to threadably receive a bolt to connect inner and outer cover plates to one another. Instead the L-shaped or U-shaped pieces are provided as described in paragraph [0032] to prevent local collapse during curing when preparing the inner filler cap 7 which itself includes the "inner filler cap interior skin 71", the "sunken inner filler cap skin 76" and the "sandwich layer 71" (which can be a "honeycomb" structure) positioned therebetween.
The secondary reference to Ramirez et al applied in combination with the BASTR EP publication to allegedly show the obviousness of providing an O-ring seal that may
be seated in a circumferential groove is noted. However, such a disclosure does not cure the deficiencies of the BASTR EP publication as discussed above.
Thus, an ordinarily skilled person in this art cannot reasonably derive the

structural features as defined in the presently pending claims from the disclosure of the BASTR EP publication. Instead, it is only the present Applicant's disclosure which provides a basis for the claims now pending herein. But "[t]he inventor's own path itself never leads to a conclusion of obviousness; that is hindsight. What matters is the path that the person of ordinary skill in the art would have followed, as evidenced by the pertinent prior art."1

Applicant therefore submits that the BASTR EP publication does not anticipate or render obvious the herein claimed invention either alone or taken with Ramirez et al. Withdrawal of all rejections advanced against the prior pending claims under 35 USC §102(a)(1) and 103 is therefore in order.
3. Conclusions
Every effort has been made to advance prosecution of this application to
allowance. Therefore in view of the amendments and comments provided to date, the Applicant submits that all pending claims are in condition for allowance.

Should any small matters be further noted that require adjustment, the Examiner is encouraged to telephone the Applicant's undersigned attorney so the same may be resolved without the need for a further written action and response.
